name: The compiler-tool assurance layer -- productize the P4 audit into a standing per-tool harness
description: Andrew-direct 2026-07-10 (via CVO brief -> CTO PRD). The 2026-07-09/10 NFRA_TOOLCHECK.P4 audit established that the directory-scoped SCANNERS generalize -- but the layer that tells you a scanner is WIRED / CATALOGUED / TESTED / TRUTHFULLY-DESCRIBED does not exist, uniformly across all ~60 tools. Every failure clustered OFF the scan: comp-surface-check is CORRECT and invoked by NO gate (17 commits touched SEV1 client-number surfaces since 06-01, gated by none); the universe is 60-on-disk / 63-by-predicate / ~42-catalogued while CLAUDE.md said ~30; 32 of 60 tools have NO test file (53%); NEVER#1 covers 2 of 3 firm-sep legs, NEVER#7's banned op runs ungated in both shells. COMPASSURANCE builds the assurance layer as a standing harness keyed on the RAIL_SET (R1-R7) the audit produced -- the 'comp-ladder': a (pipeline-layer x rail) matrix per tool, a scanner is ASSURED only when every cell has a GENERATED negative control shown able to go RED (mutant-killed). 0.8.0's mutation-tested comp-iam is the reference impl of one tool passing; the 32-untested census is the backlog. Author/verifier split is structural: CTO owns architecture, CVO stays off design to adversarially certify. PRD docs/architecture/NFRA_COMPASSURANCE.md.
